comments.author: mbenjaminsmith
comments.why_zh: 涵盖忆阻器元件、片上 CPU 内存和新的 CPU 架构
comments.quote_zh: Williams 在 YouTube 上的演讲真的很棒。
comments.text_zh: 我不明白为什么一讨论忆阻器，Leon Chua 总是第一个被提起。HP 的 Williams 才是把它变成现实的人。Chua 预言了忆阻器的存在，但据我所知，他在做出一个能工作的实例方面没有任何进展。这有点像把直升机的发明归功于达芬奇。Williams 在 YouTube 上的演讲真的很棒。他讲了这种元件本身、它在内存中的用途（作为大量片上 CPU 内存），以及基于它构建新 CPU 架构的可能性：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I don't understand why Leon Chua keeps popping up first when memristors are discussed. Williams at HP is the person that made it a reality. Chua postulated the existence of the memristor but as far as I know made no progress on a working example. That's a bit like giving da Vinci credit for the invention of the helicopter. The Williams talk on youtube is really good. He discusses the element itself, its use in memory (as vast amounts of on-CPU memory) as well as the possibility of new CPU architectures based on it: [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 忆阻器演讲，包括在处理器之上堆叠数百个芯片
comments.quote_zh: 他那场精彩的忆阻器演讲
comments.text_zh: 我们实际上可能会看到这两件事同时发生；R. Stanley Williams 在他那场精彩的忆阻器演讲中谈到的一件事，是他们开发的一种把数百个芯片堆叠在处理器之上的方法，他说这最终带来的好处可能和忆阻器本身一样大。想象一下，把一太字节甚至更多极快的非易失性存储，通过一条你想做多宽就做多宽的总线，直接连在 CPU 顶上，由此打开的可能性简直令人难以置信。然后你再想想，你可以把它们当作 FPGA 来做计算，并动态重配置它们……哇。忆阻器距离商用只有一两年了，不过要真正达到炒作中的期望，可能还需要一段时间。我们生活在激动人心的时代。演讲在这里：[VIDEO]
comments.text: We may actually see them both happening at once; one of the things R. Stanley Williams talks about in his excellent memristor talk is a method they developed for stacking hundreds of chips on top of a processor, which he says may end up providing just as much benefit as the memristor itself. The possibilities that could be opened up by having a terabyte or more of extremely fast non volatile storage attached by a bus as large as you care to make it directly on top of a CPU are mind boggling. Then when you consider that you can use them as FPGAs for computation instead and dynamically reconfigure them... wow. Memristors are only a year or two away from commercial availability, though it will probably be a while after that until they live up to the hype. We live in exciting times. The talk: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 《我如何学会不再担忧并爱上微缩化》： [VIDEO] 说真的，去看吧。忆阻器技术依赖的正是这种微缩化，并且能在当前架构的若干领域带来速度提升。其次，我在半导体行业工作过：有很多保守力量在阻碍发展。如果他们对 CMOS 工艺中一切看起来有点异乎寻常的东西——比如 high-k 电介质——不是那么过敏式地反应，我们本可以拥有比现在省心得多的现有技术。
comments.text: How i learned to stop worrying and love the miniaturization: [VIDEO] Seriously, watch it. Memristor-tech relies on this kind of miniaturization and can provide a speed boost in several areas in current architectures. Secondly, having worked for semi: there's a lot of conservative force holding back development. We could have had current tech with much less worries than we have now if they didn't respond so allergically to everything that looks a little exotic in the CMOS process, like high-k dielectrics.

comments.text: Here's a useful, but lengthy, talk on the subject: [VIDEO] Memristors look extremely likely to be able to provide non-volatile storage with latency, access speeds, and density higher than existing DRAM and flash. And those seem to be the less fascinating aspects of memristor technology.

comments.why_zh: 澄清了只有高压差下状态才会改变
comments.text_zh: 我读到这个类比时，立刻开始想：如果每次让水流动时直径都会变化，那要用这个效应会有多复杂。然后我看了 achille 发的视频 [1]。如果我没理解错视频的意思，这个类比应该说明一个关键点：只有在压力差非常高时，管道的直径才会增大或减小。你可以在低压下让水流动，而不会以任何可测量的方式影响直径。这应该会让忆阻器在实际使用中容易得多。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: I read this analogy and immediately started thinking how complicated it would be to use this effect if the diameter is always changing, every time you make your water flow. Then I watched the video posted by achille [1]. If I understood the video correctly, the analogy should specify a fundamental thing: The diameter of the pipe only increases or decreases if the pressure differential is very high. You can make your water flow at low pressure without affecting the diameter in any measurable way. This should make using memristors practically much easier. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: danmaz74
comments.story_title: With 'The Machine,' HP May Have Invented a New Kind of Computer
comments.why_zh: 演讲者说早先的论文注意到了该效应，但没联系到忆阻器
comments.text_zh: 有意思的是，这正是 HP 实验室负责人在这段视频 [1] 里说的：很多论文注意到了这个效应并讨论了异常现象，但在他们之前没人把它和忆阻器联系起来。他还说，这个效应只有在纳米尺度上才真正明显（因为它需要极高的电场）。编辑：再想想，情况并非如此，因为 HP 的忆阻器并不是最初描述它的那篇论文意义上的忆阻器——它和磁通量毫无关系。它只能用同一组方程来描述，所以它的行为像忆阻器，但并不是“真正”补全了那一组基本元件的忆阻器 [2]。也就是说，如果我正确理解了视频的话（但我觉得我理解对了，因为演讲者自己在视频开头就谈到了一个“trick”）。[1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]
comments.text: Interestingly, this is exactly what the chief of HP labs said in this video [1]: That lots of papers noted the effect and talked about anomalies, but no-one made the connection to the memristors before them. He also says that the effect is only really noticeable at nano scales (because it needs incredibly high electric fields). EDIT: on second thought, that's not the case, because the HP memristor is not a memristor in the sense of the of the original paper describing it - it has nothing to do with the magnetic flux. It can only be described with the same set of equations, so, it behaves like a memristor, but is not "actually" a memristor that completes the set [2]. That is, if I understood the video correctly (but I think I did, as the speaker himself talked about a "trick" in the beginning of the video). [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]

comments.author: danmaz74
comments.story_title: With 'The Machine,' HP May Have Invented a New Kind of Computer
comments.why_zh: 说明用短高压脉冲写入、用低压读取
comments.text_zh: 忆阻器就像磁芯存储器一样，读取是破坏性的——但在 HP 的实现里（那并不是“真正”的忆阻器），真的如此吗？在视频演讲 [1] 中，他们演示了用非常短的“高”压脉冲来改变忆阻器的状态，然后用较低的电压测量其电阻，而这些低电压不会让氧空位迁移——因此不会改变状态，如果我理解得没错的话。如果他们能用这些低电压（和低电流）有效地读取状态而不改变它，那他们就能得到极其简化的存储器管理，以及功耗极低的读取操作，这也能证明他们的说法：他们的忆阻器可以堆叠成 3D 而不产生散热问题。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: memristors, like core memory, are destructively read but are they really, with HP implementation - which is not a "real" memristor? In the video presentation [1] they show that they change the state of the memristor using very short "high" voltage impulses, and then measure its resistance using lower voltages that do not make the oxygen vacancies migrate - and thus do not change the state, if I understood that correctly. If they can use these low voltages (and low currents) to effectively read the state without altering it, they get incredibly simplified management of the memory, and incredibly low power read operations, which would justify their assertion that their memristors can be packed in 3d without thermal problems. [1] [VIDEO]
